thesis.v: Goodwill already operates an attended donation center (ADC) at 1311 Stony Point Road in the Pantops retail node, near the US-250/Route 20 intersection — this evaluates expanding that presence into a full store, which is what "Pantops Expansion Potential" refers to in the underlying email thread. Pantops is Goodwill's stated top Charlottesville-area target (per Jackson Green's 8/17 email): strong brand recognition locally, a long-standing presence, and the dominant intersection in the area. Their open concern is customer stop-ability at a site visible from a busy highway (US-250) — they cite two underperforming Goodwill locations elsewhere with that same profile — though they believe Pantops' brand strength and traffic volume outweigh that risk. The vacant 47,550 SF former Roses box at Pantops Shopping Center (400 Pantops Center, dark since March 2025) is a notable nearby alternative in the same node worth tracking, though it's larger than Goodwill's typical 15,000–25,000 SF format. No financing model or development scenario has been built for either site yet — this card is basic property information only, per Ben's 8/19 request.

flags.text: Goodwill's brand in Charlottesville/Albemarle "ranks extremely high" per Jackson Green (Goodwill CFO), and they've had a presence in the Pantops area for years — strong customer-acceptance case despite US-250 visibility concerns raised for other markets.

Pantops sits at "THE primary intersection in this entire Pantops area" (Jackson Green, 8/17 email) — US-250 at Route 20 (Stony Point Rd), which VDOT is actively studying for intersection/corridor reconstruction, a sign of sustained growth pressure.

The 47,550 SF former Roses box at Pantops Shopping Center (400 Pantops Center) has been vacant since March 2025; the owner (Great Eastern Management Co.) has said they'd rather find a tenant than redevelop — worth a call even though it's larger than Goodwill's typical format.

Goodwill's own stated risk (Jackson Green): stores visible from busy/congested roads have underperformed elsewhere in their portfolio (cites Orange Ave East in Roanoke, Rt. 220 in Bassett) — they believe Pantops' brand strength offsets this, but it's their explicit diligence question, not ours.

Goodwill is also weighing cross-cannibalization against its existing Mill Creek and Rt. 29 North stores — they believe Charlottesville's neighborhood "clusters" (Pantops pulls from Glenmore/Keswick; Mill Creek pulls from Downtown/5th Street) limit overlap, but this is their internal read, not independently verified here.
